newsitem.title: USA: Medicare payments to US HMOs to rise 5.9 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Medicare payments to US HMOs to rise 5.9 pct in 97.

text.p: Medicare payment rates to health maintenance organizations will rise by an average of 5.9 percent next year, compared with a 10.1 percent rise in 1996, the U.S. Health Care Finance Administration said.
The 5.9 percent figure for 1997 is down from an estimate of 7.2 percent that had been announced in July because of changed hospital payment estimates.

"While the formula for setting the rates still needs to be changed, the 1997 rates demonstrate the Medicare payment rates for managed care plans are moving in parallel with private sector payments," said HCFA administrator Bruce Vladeck.

Rates are set for each county, following a national formula for AAPCC (average adjusted per capita cost). The highest monthly rate if $767.35 for Richmond County, N.Y., while the lowest rate is $220.92 in Arthur County, Nebraska.

Managed care plans get paid 95 percent of their county's AAPCC rates. During the inconclusive debate over Medicare reform last year, there was considerable argument over how to change that formula, and whether HMOS were getting paid more than they should be.
About 4.5 million of the 37 million Medicare beneficiaries are in managed care plans such as HMOs.
